ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing and ongoing screening of every UBO, director, officer, and authorized signatory against the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions lists; OFAC SDN/Consolidated List (required by correspondent banks for USD settlement); Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and Criminal Code s 83.05 (terrorist entities); FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) and head-of-international-organization (HIO) screening under PCMLTFA reporting obligations; enhanced due diligence triggered by acceptance of USDC crypto tokens — FATF Recommendation 15 and FINTRAC Retail Payment Activities Act guidance, including sanctions blockchain address screening and wallet attribution analysis; all PEP matches require senior management approval and, where threshold criteria are met, FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting within prescribed timelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Access online portal (https://www.albertacorporateaccess.gov.ab.ca) operated by Service Alberta; NUANS reports obtainable through accredited private service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or French (or a combination), using the 26-letter Latin alphabet; accented characters and non-Latin scripts require transliteration into English/French at filing. The name must consist of a distinctive element, an optional descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element. For an Alberta ULC, the legal element must be one of: 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', 'Societe a Responsabilite Illimitee', or 'SRI' (English/French formulations); the French forms may use unaccented characters per registry practice. Numbers and letters are permitted; misleadingly geographic names require consent or a certificate of extra-provincial registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon NUANS rejection (distinctiveness failure or confusing similarity), the applicant may: (1) file a written reconsideration request with the Alberta Corporate Registry through the Corporate Access portal within 30 days of rejection, attaching rebuttal evidence; (2) if the registry maintains the refusal, file an originating application to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act for judicial review of the registrar's decision, with a 30-day administrative law limitation period; (3) concurrently request an extension of the NUANS report validity by submitting a new name reservation filing within the original 90-day window; and (4) for trademark-based rejections or third-party oppositions, initiate statutory proceeding under the Trade-marks Act before the Federal Court of Canada — registry-level third-party opposition does not exist in Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible — a pure mail-forwarding virtual office without a physical Alberta location is not acceptable; ABCA s 101(1) and s 22 require a registered office and registered records office physically located in Alberta at street-address level (no post office box) where process can be served and statutory records are accessible. A 'virtual office' product with a physical commercial suite, live reception, and an Alberta-licensed registered agent accepting service of process is permissible and is the recommended commercial substance solution for an AI/LLM API platform with no local employees. The registered records office must be open during business hours for inspection of specified corporate records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — annualized probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is estimated at 3-5% for a standard-risk, license-exempt software/AI corporation. Service Alberta does not routinely inspect registered offices of ordinary commercial corporations, but inspections may occur upon complaints, returned mail, or registry integrity checks; adoption of an agent-based physical registered office reduces this probability to near-zero. If the ULC later handles USDC custody or transfer unaccompanied by a regulated payment intermediary, FINTRAC compliance examinations and site visits would elevate the inspection risk materially.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended — ss 6–17 (articles of incorporation), s 101 (registered office), s 113 (officers), and Division governing unlimited liability corporations: shareholders' liability imposed by the articles; supplementary governance under the Alberta Corporate Registry Interpretation Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Ministry of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed online via the Corporate Registry Portal; Certificate of Incorporation issued as conclusive evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; a ULC may be incorporated with nil or nominal capital subscribed, and shares issued at CAD 0.01 per share; subscription proceeds are credited to the ULC bank account.

Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at [Address], Alberta; [Agent] is appointed records office. 3. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — NUANS search through accredited service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two or three proposed corporate names including the suffix 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'; obtain a NUANS report valid for 90 days; no notarization required; attach written consents for sensitive names.
required_dossiers: Consent letter for conflicting or regulated-name terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a fresh NUANS search with alternative names or submit a consent letter from the conflicting party; resubmit within the report's validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — online Corporate Registry Portal or paper counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation: name, registered office in Alberta, share structure (100 unlimited common shares), the express unlimited liability provision, and directors; sign electronically and pay the CAD 350 filing fee; Certificate of Incorporation is issued after statutory review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a Corporate Registry deficiency query within the stated deadline by resubmitting corrected schedules; minor errors are cured through a filing for Certificate of Amendment or Notice of Correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — document retrieval and records services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the official Certificate of Incorporation; establish the corporate minute book, securities register, and common seal; issue subscriber share certificates and record transfers in the register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a re-issued certificate at the registry counter; correct minor registry errors by filing a Notice of Correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Records Address Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — corporate records administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office address in Alberta as stated in the Articles; appoint the records address (may be the same), satisfying the requirement to keep share and meeting records accessible in the province.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a Notice of Change of Registered Office or Records Address upon any relocation; late notices are accepted with a late-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Written Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or execute written resolutions covering share subscription, registered office confirmation, officer appointments, banking mandates, and tax classification decisions; record minutes in the minute book.
required_dossiers: Minutes of first board meeting or written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If procedural defects surface, pass a unanimous ratification and consent resolution signed by all directors and shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notice of Directors and Officers to the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prescribed Notice of Directors identifying each director and officer; include residential addresses and signed consents; update the registry within 15 days of any change.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an amended Notice of Directors upon administrative review; a correction submission to the registry resolves incomplete or inaccurate data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal CRA Registration (Business Number and Tax Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated ULC with the CRA to obtain a nine-digit Business Number; register for GST/HST where taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 (annual universal threshold); open a payroll (RP) account when employees are engaged; document ULC pass-through classification for income tax.
required_dossiers: Estimated annual revenue and payroll data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration data is incomplete or rejected, re-file electronically or lodge a written adjustment request with the CRA Business Window; corrections are generally processed within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or City of Edmonton (applicable Alberta municipality) business license office and fire department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general office business license under the municipal Business License By-law; schedule a fire inspection per the Alberta Fire Code; obtain an occupancy permit for the office premises; no industrial manufacturing or code-related authorization is required for an AI/LLM API software operation.
required_dossiers: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) compliance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify municipal deficiency letters by submitting floor plans, fire-extinguisher certificates, and landlord compliance documents; re-inspection is scheduled within ten business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board governs office-based AI/LLM API providers; municipal planning and building authorities are the relevant administrative gatekeepers.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no statutory operating permit for ISIC 6201); municipal general business license and occupancy permit are the operative permits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based generative AI and API software operations do not appear on the mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment activity list; registration may only be triggered by physical data centers with backup generators, in which case municipal air/electrical permits apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions generated; office sewage discharges conform to municipal sewer by-laws; discarded servers and e-waste must be handled by an Alberta-registered recycler under the Recycling Regulation (Alberta).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code inspection required: exit routes, extinguishers, and fire alarm verification; structural load certification for server racks; OHS workplace clearance covering ergonomic workstations and electrical safety; provincial workers' compensation (WCB) coverage mandatory when employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), national tax authority administering federal and provincial taxes including Alberta via canada.ca/revenue-agency
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register for a Business Number (BN) with CRA if carrying on business in Canada; GST/HST registration required if taxable supplies exceed $30,000 annually. Submit via My Business Account or Form RC0001.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; taxation follows legal corporate form. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under Income Tax Act Part XIII.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: GST/HST returns filed electronically via My Business Account; no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandated, but detailed records must be retained for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST/HST zero-rated on exports of goods and offshore services to non-residents where service is not consumed in Canada. Goods require proof of export from Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract penalties up to 200% of tax involved, interest, and potential criminal prosecution; refunds subject to retrospective clawback upon audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration is split between the Minister of Finance, the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for reporting, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for bank supervision, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money-laundering and countering terrorist financing (AML/CTF) supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. There are no general exchange control restrictions on dividend distributions, interest payments, management fees, or repatriation of share capital. Profit remittance from an Alberta ULC is legally unrestricted provided the entity remains in good standing, remittances are supported by documented corporate resolutions and arm's-length pricing where applicable, and payment instructions comply with sanctions administered by Global Affairs Canada. Capital account inflows, including non-resident equity injections, are freely admitted, but large transactions may trigger FINTRAC reporting thresholds (C$10,000 or more) and prompt source-of-funds verification at the receiving financial institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed holding period for export receipts in Canada. A Canadian exporter may retain foreign currency in offshore or domestic foreign-currency-denominated bank accounts; any foreign exchange gain or loss is subject to Canadian tax principles, and the CRA may require business records establishing the source and disposition of received funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Cross-Border Foreign Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low–Medium as a primary treasury rail, but viable as a supplementary collection route. Offshore digital EMI or e-money institutions do not hold a Canadian bank license and cannot legally accept deposits in Canada or provide Canadian domestic payment functionality in the manner of a Schedule I or Schedule II bank. Such EMIs may supply card issuing, merchant acquiring, and crypto-fiat conversion services through partner banks; however OSFI, FINTRAC, and the Bank of Canada impose clear boundaries: any entity that undertakes Canadian deposit-taking or retail payment activity must be authorized under the Bank Act or the Retail Payment Activities Act, as applicable. For a CA-AB ULC whose target rails include USDC, a Canadian Tier-1 bank account should remain the principal liquidity trunk, with an authorized Canadian fintech or a foreign EMI used only for tokenized exposure and API-billing collection, never for custody of gross settlement balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks generally require at least one director, or a designated senior officer with authority, to complete an in-person or live video identity verification for the corporate account. Physical attendance at a branch is not an absolute statutory mandate for every signatory, but Schedule I banks in practice require the beneficial owner(s) and controlling directors to undergo a verified identity interview, preferably in Canada. For non-resident directors of an Alberta ULC, remote opening is possible where the bank uses an approved digital identity verification provider, but the ULC must demonstrate a local registered office, Alberta corporate registry extracts, and valid director identification. Letters of authorization may allow a corporate secretary or local representative to conduct onboarding, subject to the bank's enhanced due diligence and the requirement that at least the ultimate beneficial owner be disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership concentration in high-risk or sanctions-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta corporate registry certificate and good standing extract; full organizational chart tracing all shareholders to ultimate natural persons; certified passport and proof of residential address for each UBO; OSFI-compliant source-of-wealth declaration; corroborating audited or reviewed financial statements for the ULC; and an independent sanctions and PEP screening report from a recognized third-party diligence provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency-linked funding sources or high-frequency USDC settlement flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed treasury narrative classifying each inbound capital injection as equity, loan, or API platform revenue; on-chain transaction trail and exchange-generated statements for USDC conversions; signed attestation that no funds are derived from unregulated gambling, darknet, ransomware, or mixer services; a formal AML risk assessment for the AI-API commercial model; and audited financial statements demonstrating that fiat and crypto treasury flows reconcile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared ISIC business activity and actual SWIFT payment purpose codes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master subscription agreement for LLM inference services; platform usage analytics and billing records; standard contractual milestones; invoices referencing ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511; contract descriptions matching 'generative AI API access, model inference, token-based AI LLM services'; and a technical services description letter from the ULC's legal counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or politically exposed person identified among directors or shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening result; explanation of commercial legitimacy; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation; independent legal opinion on the ownership structure; bank-specific enhanced due diligence questionnaire; and confirmation that the PEP is not a foreign politically exposed person subject to heightened risk without an approved relationship-management sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction velocity and low average ticket size inconsistent with payroll/corporate expense profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cap table, subscription list, and customer concentration report; API pricing schedule and token billing records; treasury policy stating cash-concentration practices; outsourced payroll provider contract showing monthly net settlement cycles; and pro forma cash-flow projections demonstrating that inbound revenues map to subscription settlements and outbound payments map to compute, data, and payroll obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound shareholder equity from non-resident investors is: (1) instruct the remitting bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 using the Alberta ULC as beneficiary, with the remittance information field reading 'Alberta ULC share subscription—[Director Resolution Date]' or 'ALBERTA ULC SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION'; (2) ensure the originating bank, intermediary bank, and beneficiary bank screening systems identify no sanctions exposure; (3) post funds to a dedicated capital escrow account before moving to the operating account; (4) provide the receiving Canadian bank with the corporate resolution authorizing the share issuance, the shareholder register update, a completed Canadian source-of-funds questionnaire, and bank reference from the remitting institution; (5) where a designated 'purpose code' is required by the correspondent bank, use a generic trade or investment purpose code consistent with 'shares and participating interests' under the Joint Message Type guidelines, or use the equivalent cross-border capital purpose code accepted by the receiving Canadian institution. Canada does not maintain a statutory foreign-exchange purpose-code regime, but banks apply counterparty screening and FINTRAC record-keeping for all transfers of C$10,000 or greater.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for outbound trade, infrastructure, and operational settlement from an Alberta ULC are: SWIFT MT103 for fiat payments to vendors, distributors, cloud service providers, and overseas contractors; SWIFT MT202 for interbank treasury reallocation where needed; Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary LCs) for high-value goods and equipment imports, with issue and confirmation routed through a Tier-1 Canadian bank; centrally cleared Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) and Real-Time Rail (RTR) or Lynx for Canadian-dollar domestic obligations; and bank-integrated foreign-currency accounts to accumulate USD and other currencies, reducing conversion cost. Outbound disbursements must be supported by an underlying commercial agreement, pro forma invoice where applicable, board-authorized delegation of payment instructions, and sanctions screening of all counterparties and intermediary beneficiaries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter (OTC) plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards with a Canadian Schedule I bank for USD/CAD and other major currency pairs
Cross-currency swaps executed under an ISDA Master Agreement where the ULC has an identified future stream of USD-denominated API revenue and CAD-denominated payroll or infrastructure costs
FX options, specifically European-style dollar-Canadian and dollar-major currency options, purchased for asymmetric downside protection on trade settlement exposures

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the underlying settlement currency is non-convertible or offshore-convertibility restrictions exist; for liquid Canadian-dollar and US-dollar markets, deliverable forwards are preferred
Interest rate and currency basis swaps used solely to hedge contracted capital project or licensing cash flows, documented at the entity level rather than for speculative treasury purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation (e.g., May 15 incorporation = July 14 due date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late-fee schedule; after a Registrar default notice, failure to cure for 3 months or more triggers administrative dissolution and a revival application with reinstatement fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and written shareholder resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Minute book of the corporation (no external filing; AGM date declared on the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; later AGMs at intervals not exceeding 15 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered winding-up on the Director's application for non-compliance; the annual return cannot be certified with a valid AGM date, exposing the ULC to administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register — annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Service Alberta (register retained at the registered office; accuracy declared on the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register update within 15 days of any share transfer or control change; annual confirmation with the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence liability of CAD 5,000 for individuals and CAD 25,000 for corporations for false or omitted ISC entries; immediate production of the register required upon Registrar or enforcement-official demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 corporation income tax return and AT1 Alberta corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (T2) and Alberta Corporate Tax Office (AT1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus 6 months for filing; final balance due 2 months after year-end (non-Canadian-controlled ULC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, capped at 12 months; gross-negligence penalties under section 163(2) of the Income Tax Act for repeated or wilful failure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and minute book compilation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretary and board of directors (no government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after fiscal year-end and before the annual-return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain statutory registers is an offence under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); directors are liable to compensate the corporation for fraudulent or negligent record-keeping

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return (when annual filing election is in force)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (annual filer); quarterly filers remit by the end of the month following the quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% plus 1% per month, up to 12 months; arrears interest compounded daily; GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold under the Alberta BCA; an auditor is required solely when the ULC is a distributing corporation or when shareholders decline to pass a unanimous waiver. A private ULC may waive the auditor every financial year by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public accountability; ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private ULCs. A U.S. check-the-box pass-through election does not alter Canadian financial-statement obligations. Income-tax books and records are kept for 6 years after the end of the taxation year; charter and register books are kept for the life of the corporation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not impose a separate annual UBO filing. The ULC maintains an ISC register identifying every individual with 25% or more voting rights or beneficial ownership, de facto control, or the power to elect or remove a majority of directors; any share transfer or control change must be recorded within 15 days; the annual return declares the register accurate and current.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 185 - 550 USD per year (CAD 250 - 750) depending on agent profile and service level
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 USD with a unanimous auditor waiver; 5,600 - 15,000 USD (CAD 7,500 - 20,000) per engagement when an audit is mandatory or shareholder-required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (15% federal Part I rate + 8% Alberta corporate income tax rate, combined general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for AI/LLM SaaS platforms. Preferential rules include: (i) the federal small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs), reducing the combined federal/Alberta rate to 11% on the first C$500,000 of active business income; (ii) refundable Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits, equal to 35% of qualified current expenditures for CCPCs and 15% non-refundable for other corporations; (iii) the Alberta Research and Development Tax Credit, generally 10% non-refundable on eligible Alberta R&D expenditures; (iv) accelerated capital cost allowance on eligible computer hardware, software, and data processing equipment used in the AI infrastructure.
